mcqs.question: Which of the following ray diagrams correctly shows the formation of a real, inverted image of a distant object by a convex lens?

options.A: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the focal point after refraction, and a ray through the optical centre passes straight; the two rays intersect on the opposite side forming an inverted image.
options.B: A ray through the focal point emerges parallel to the principal axis, and a ray through the centre passes straight; the rays intersect on the same side forming a virtual image.
options.C: Both rays pass through the optical centre only, meeting at the centre of the lens; no image is formed.
options.D: A ray through the focal point emerges through the centre, and a ray parallel to the axis passes through the centre; the rays intersect on the same side forming an upright image.

mcqs.answer: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the focal point after refraction, and a ray through the optical centre passes straight; the two rays intersect on the opposite side forming an inverted image.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens, a ray parallel to the principal axis refracts through the principal focus on the image side, while a ray passing through the optical centre continues undeviated. Their intersection gives the real, inverted image. Options B, C and D describe situations that produce virtual or no images, which are incorrect for a real image of a distant object.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 15 cm in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 10 cm. What is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.A: Real, inverted image formed 6 cm behind the lens.
options.B: Virtual, upright image formed 6 cm behind the lens.
options.C: Real, upright image formed 6 cm in front of the lens.
options.D: Virtual, inverted image formed 6 cm in front of the lens.

mcqs.answer: Real, inverted image formed 6 cm behind the lens.
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (with u = -15 cm, f = +10 cm), we get 1/v = 1/10 - (-1/15) = 0.1667, so v = +6 cm. Positive v indicates a real image on the opposite side of the lens, and the image is inverted. Hence option A is correct; the other options describe virtual or upright images which do not match the calculation.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about convex and concave lenses?

options.A: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a real focus on the image side.
options.B: A concave lens diverges parallel rays as if they originated from a virtual focus on the object side.
options.C: A convex lens can produce a virtual, upright image of a distant object.
options.D: A concave lens can produce a real, inverted image of an object placed beyond its focal length.

mcqs.answer: A concave lens can produce a real, inverted image of an object placed beyond its focal length.
mcqs.explanation: Concave lenses always produce virtual, upright, reduced images regardless of object position; they never form real, inverted images. Therefore statement D is false. Statements A, B and C are correct descriptions of lens behavior.

mcqs.question: The optical centre of a thin lens is defined as the point through which:

options.A: The principal axis intersects the lens surface.
options.B: A ray passes without any deviation.
options.C: The focal length is measured from.
options.D: The image distance equals the object distance.

mcqs.answer: A ray passes without any deviation.
mcqs.explanation: In a thin lens, the optical centre (also called the principal point) is the point where a ray passing through it emerges undeviated. This property is used in ray diagrams. Options A, C and D describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the principal focus of a convex lens with that of a concave lens?

options.A: The principal focus of a convex lens lies on the same side as the object, whereas for a concave lens it lies on the opposite side.
options.B: Both lenses have their principal focus on the side opposite to the incoming light.
options.C: The principal focus of a convex lens is real and located on the image side, while that of a concave lens is virtual and located on the object side.
options.D: Both lenses have a virtual principal focus.

mcqs.answer: The principal focus of a convex lens is real and located on the image side, while that of a concave lens is virtual and located on the object side.
mcqs.explanation: A convex (converging) lens has a real focal point on the side where the image forms. A concave (diverging) lens has a virtual focal point on the same side as the object, from which refracted rays appear to diverge. Option C captures this distinction; the other options misstate the locations or nature of the focal points.

mcqs.question: A thin convex lens forms a real, inverted image of a candle that is twice the size of the object. If the object is placed 30 cm from the lens, what is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: Magnification m = -v/u = -2 (image twice size, inverted). Hence v = 2u = 60 cm (positive for real image). Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = 1/60 + 1/30 = 3/60 = 1/20, we obtain f = 20 cm. Option C is correct; the other values do not satisfy the lens formula with the given magnification.

mcqs.question: Which ray diagram correctly shows the formation of a virtual, upright image by a concave lens for an object placed beyond its focal length?

options.A: A ray parallel to the principal axis diverges as if originating from the focal point on the object's side, and a ray through the optical centre passes straight; the extensions of the refracted rays meet on the object's side forming a virtual, upright image.
options.B: A ray through the focal point emerges parallel to the principal axis, and a ray through the centre passes straight; the rays intersect on the image side forming a real image.
options.C: Both rays pass through the optical centre only, meeting at the centre of the lens; no image is formed.
options.D: A ray through the centre emerges through the focal point, and a ray parallel to the axis passes through the centre; the rays intersect on the image side forming an inverted image.

mcqs.answer: A ray parallel to the principal axis diverges as if originating from the focal point on the object's side, and a ray through the optical centre passes straight; the extensions of the refracted rays meet on the object's side forming a virtual, upright image.
mcqs.explanation: For a concave (diverging) lens, a ray parallel to the principal axis appears to diverge from the virtual focus on the object's side, while a ray through the optical centre is undeviated. Extending these refracted rays backward gives the location of a virtual, upright, reduced image. Options B, C, and D describe situations that either produce real images or no image, which are incorrect for a concave lens.

mcqs.question: If an object is placed exactly at the focal point of a convex lens, what is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.A: Real, inverted image formed at the focal length on the opposite side.
options.B: Virtual, upright image formed at twice the focal length on the same side.
options.C: No image is formed; refracted rays are parallel and the image is at infinity.
options.D: Real, upright image formed at the focal point on the opposite side.

mcqs.answer: No image is formed; refracted rays are parallel and the image is at infinity.
mcqs.explanation: When an object is placed at the focal point of a convex lens, rays after refraction emerge parallel to each other, never meeting to form a real image. The image is said to form at infinity. Hence option C is correct. Options A, B, and D incorrectly describe image formation that does not occur in this situation.
